title: Intel Nova Lake die shots show TSMC N2P being used for compute die, 18A-P for SoC Hub and Peripheral dies
gist: Leaked bare-die shots of Intel's Nova Lake-HX and Nova Lake-H laptop chips show a six-die package where only the CPU compute tile is on TSMC N2P, while the hub and peripheral dies use Intel 18A-P and the GPU tile uses Intel 3-E. Roughly 40% of silicon area in the HX part is dummy or passive filler, and the compute tile is a minority of total area.

insights.claim: Intel's Nova Lake-HX and Nova Lake-H mobile chips put the main CPU compute tile (P-cores and E-cores) on an external foundry, TSMC's N2P node, rather than on Intel's own process.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Intel's highest-performance CPU cores in this generation depend on TSMC capacity, a revenue win for TSMC and a signal on Intel Foundry's competitiveness for leading-edge compute.
insights.quote: Finally, Intel uses an external foundry for the main compute tile, which is on the TSMC N2P node
insights.locator: Finally, Intel uses an external foundry

insights.claim: Intel's own 18A-P node is used for the lower-performance-sensitive silicon (the central hub die hosting 4 LPE-cores and the peripheral control tile) rather than for the P/E-core compute tile.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Suggests Intel is placing 18A-P on supporting dies first and keeping the flagship compute on TSMC, which tempers the read on 18A-P's readiness for high-performance cores.
insights.locator: Next, there is a large 72 mm² die

insights.claim: The same TSMC N2P compute tile approach spans both the 8P+16E HX and 4P+8E H variants, so TSMC N2P supplies Intel across at least two mobile SKUs, with 104 mm² and 55 mm² compute tiles respectively.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: N2P volume demand from Intel scales with SKU mix; the larger HX tile consumes nearly twice the N2P area of the H tile.
insights.locator: Next, we move to the less powerful

insights.claim: Nova Lake-HX is a six-die package spanning three different process nodes (Intel 3-E graphics, Intel 18A-P hub and peripheral, TSMC N2P compute), plus dummy and passive structural dies.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Node-per-function disaggregation lets Intel mix its own and foundry capacity, but raises packaging and supply-chain complexity.
insights.quote: divided across six different dies manufactured on various nodes
insights.locator: The total silicon size measures 12x30 mm

insights.claim: The Nova Lake-HX package totals 360 mm2 of silicon in a 12x30 mm footprint, yet the compute tile is only 104 mm2, so well under a third of the area is the leading-edge compute die.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Leading-edge wafer area per package is a fraction of total silicon, which limits how much N2P wafer demand each Intel chip generates.
insights.locator: The total silicon size measures 12x30 mm

insights.claim: Dummy and passive structural dies (21 mm2 and 85 mm2) make up roughly 106 mm2 of the HX package, around 30% of the stated 360 mm2 silicon area, used for package structural integrity.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Substantial filler silicon points to cost and area overhead in chiplet packaging and to where cost-down or layout optimization could come.
insights.locator: Adjacent to it is a dummy die

insights.claim: Nova Lake-H is a smaller 12x23 mm, 276 mm2 package whose only differences from HX are a smaller compute tile (55 mm2 for 4P+8E) and a smaller passive die (45 mm2); the graphics, hub and peripheral dies on Intel nodes are identical.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Reusing the Intel-made dies across SKUs means only the TSMC compute tile and filler change per tier, which simplifies Intel's own fab loading.
insights.locator: Next, we move to the less powerful

insights.claim: The graphics tile is a small die of about 26 mm2 on Intel 3-E with only 4 Xe GPU cores, so integrated graphics in these HX and H parts are a minor part of the package.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Integrated GPU capability is modest, implying the HX and H tier targets discrete-GPU systems.
insights.locator: The first die is the graphics tile

insights.claim: Intel is expected to give Nova Lake-HX laptop chips the four-digit Core Ultra 4000 naming used on desktop, while H-series and suffix-less mobile chips keep the three-digit naming of the previous generation.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Naming signals product segmentation: HX is positioned with desktop silicon rather than the mainstream mobile lineup, which matters for channel and OEM mix.
insights.locator: From previous rumors, we have learned

insights.claim: HX mobile chips have traditionally been BGA versions of Intel's desktop silicon, so Intel appears to be grouping Nova Lake-HX with desktop Nova Lake-S rather than with the other laptop chips.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: If HX shares desktop silicon, TSMC N2P compute volume is tied to the desktop and high-end laptop cycle rather than to mainstream mobile.
insights.quote: HX chips have traditionally been BGA versions of Intel's desktop silicon

insights.claim: The die-shot details come from a YouTube leak channel (Moore's Law Is Dead) relayed through TechPowerUp, and the post pairs them with earlier rumors, so node assignments and naming are unconfirmed by Intel.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Treat node-allocation conclusions as rumor-grade until Intel or TSMC confirms them.

insights.claim: The itemized die areas for HX (26+21+72+58+104+85 mm2) sum to about 366 mm2 versus the stated 360 mm2 total, a small inconsistency suggesting the area figures are estimates measured from images.
insights.speaker: F
insights.so_what: Die-size figures are approximate, so derived wafer-area or cost estimates carry error.
insights.locator: The total silicon size measures 12x30 mm
